No it isn't, haha! We don't have anywhere close to the level of understanding in chemistry or physics we would need in order to be capable of describing complex organisms in those terms. What we have right now is an understanding of quarks into subatomic particles (neutrons and protons) into atoms into molecules into DNA sequences, which is transcribed to RNA and then either processed into an RNA product or more famously translated into a protein product. We can do that for ONE protein at a time, or if we're lucky we can find an enzyme complex or some other collection of multiple proteins, or some trend whereby we can see multiple genes in the same light. But we're nowhere close to understanding biology through the scope of chemistry- there are proteins we know the functions of for example but we have no idea where in the genome their respective nucleotide sequence is, or even what they would look like.
